Title: (LSJ) Sonja Blue vs On the Qui Vive

Messages.Author: floppyzedolfin
Messages.Body:
Hello :)

Here's this week's question :
If Sonja Blue wants to block as an ally, and plays On the Qui Vive;
will she untap "as normal" during my next untap phase ?

I suppose she does not, because OtqV's "If this minion is an ally, he
or she does not untap as normal during his or her next untap phase" is
somehow resolved when the card is played, and not during the untap
phase (where she would have returned to Vampire life", so her
"allyness" would be checked when the card is played, and not during
the untap phase.

I'm sure some could argue that a present tense is used in "does not
untap" form, instead of a future tense ("will not untap"), but all I
want to know it the answer ;-)

Relevant cardtexts :

Sonja Blue
She may block as an ally (but remains a vampire in combat).

On the Qui Vive
Only usable by a tapped minion. This reacting minion can play reaction
cards and attempt to block as though untapped until the current action
is concluded. If this minion is an ally, he or she does not untap as
normal during his or her next untap phase. A minion may play only one
On the Qui Vive between his or her untap phases.

Given that Sonja can play WWEF as a vampire and still block as an
ally, there's no reason to think that any hypothetical distinguishing
card can't be played as a vampire too.

I'm pretty sure Sonja's text is just the ability to block DtD and
other vampires-can't-block type effects - she couldn't play an ally-
only wake-type effect if there were one. It doesn't say block or play
reaction cards as an ally, just block as an ally.

I'll take that as an official answer then:D

But you know from a logical standpoint:

Sonja is able to block actions that are modified by Daring the Dawn
because of her special ability... as some pointed out it seems like
the most obvious intent of her ability.

Sonja is also likewise able to block actions modified by Eyes of the
Serpent because she's a vampire.

If the rules logic is that these two events are independent, it would
conclude that she would be able to block, since she "defeats" each
modifier separately, not together. The question becomes whether if the
modifiers should be interpreted independently or together.

Should all modifiers be interpreted together, or is it a case by case
thing? Obviously some modifiers "stack" together, but there isn't
anything in the wording of either Daring the Dawn or Eyes of the
Serpent to imply that they "stack" with each other.

Cheers,

Dai

You're looking at it the wrong way. Sonja either blocks as a vampire or
as an ally, not both or neither. If she's blocking as a vampire, then she
can block the Eyes of the Serpent action, but not the Daring the Dawn
action. If she's blocking as an ally, the opposite is true. I imagine
the controller of Sonja makes the choice at the appropriate time (since
she "may block as an ally"). In other words, she can't block an action
that is modified by both Eyes of the Serpent and Daring the Dawn. Go nuts
with your crazy deck!

I would also assume that she can choose not to block as an ally. Say, for
example, a bleed is modified by Daring the Dawn, she could choose to be a
vampire blocker, fail to block and Deflect it, although she was attempting
to block before DTD was played. Is that right or would her controller
have to declare her attempt to block as a vampire ahead of time? This of
course begs the question of whether Sonja could change her mind and start
blocking as an ally in the event the bleed is bounced back to her
controller.

Matt Morgan

Of course. Blocking is optional.

She may choose not to block.
She may choose to block (as the vampire she is).
Or she can use her special and attempt to block as an ally could.

> for example, a bleed is modified by Daring the Dawn, she could choose to
> be a vampire blocker, fail to block and Deflect it, although she was
> attempting to block before DTD was played.

Assuming she hadn't invoked her special prior to the DtD, yeah.

> Is that right or would her
> controller have to declare her attempt to block as a vampire ahead of
> time? This of course begs the question of whether Sonja could change
> her mind and start blocking as an ally in the event the bleed is bounced
